newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro court says Sofia violated ex-premier's rights.
newsitem.headline: Euro court says Sofia violated ex-premier's rights.

text.p: The European Court of Human Rights ruled on Thursday that Bulgaria wrongly detained late prime minister Andrei Lukanov in 1992 on suspicion of misappropriating funds.
The nine-judge court awarded Lukanov's widow and two children damages and legal costs after ruling unanimously that Bulgaria had violated Lukanov's rights to liberty and security.

Socialist Lukanov, gunned down in an unsolved murder outside his home in Sofia last year, was detained for six months in 1992 after a Bulgarian prosecutor launched an inquiry into whether he diverted funds when he was deputy prime minister in the 1980s.

He was suspected of misappropriating cash in decisions over aid totalling $34.59 million and 27.02 million levs ($17,000 at current rates) from Bulgaria to developing countries ranging from Cuba to Afghanistan.
The Bulgarian National Assembly lifted his immmunity to allow his detention but the charges were subsequently dropped.

The European Court said Bulgarian authorities had provided no evidence that Lukanov was "reasonably suspected of having sought for himself or a third party an advantage from his participation in the allocation of funds in question".

"The court did not find that the deprivation of the applicant's liberty during the period under consideration was 'lawful detention' effected 'on reasonable suspicion of (his) having committed an offence,'" a statement added.

The court, a branch of the 40-nation Council of Europe, awarded Lukanov's widow and two children a total of 40,000 French francs ($7,080) as well as costs and expenses of $13,456 and 7,067 francs ($1,250).
Lukanov, who served as prime minister for six months after ousting communist dictator Todor Zhivkov in November 1989, repeatedly appealed to be freed during his detention.

At the time of his death, Lukanov was a deputy of the Socialist party and an influential businessman. Colleagues in the divided Socialist party have said Lukanov was about to expose high-level government sleaze.
